Two reasons, one inherited and one this unit sharpens. Inherited: invariant 5.3 forces the promote verb to be deployed to ~/.claude/local/ outside every release, so its deployed copy's version is recorded nowhere and a hand-patch would survive a refresh undetected. Sharpened: settings.json is now permanently a live file that no release reproduces, removed on both branches of buildRelease (scripts/config/release.mjs:36 and :67) and again at scripts/config/promote.mjs:43, which is decision 0270's intent but is exactly M6's hand-patched-deployed-file shape - a refresh cannot regenerate it from committed source at a recorded sha. G4 names a settings file as a guardrail file, and this unit widens where one is deleted: scripts/config/release.mjs:6-15 defines stripSettings, called on the freshly extracted subtree at :67, on a release directory reused from disk at :36, and from scripts/config/promote.mjs:43 on every pointer swap, which is the path rollback takes too. The deletion is bounded and cannot reach the live guardrail - its argument is always releaseDir(configRoot, sha) or a releases/<sha>.tmp staging tree, and swapPointer re-tests sha against SHA_PATTERN at scripts/config/promote.mjs:40-42 before deriving that path, so it can only ever address <configRoot>/releases/<40-hex>/settings.json and never <configRoot>/settings.json - and every test drives a mkdtemp sandbox seeded at scripts/config/tests/_fixture.mjs:42-64, never a real home. This round narrows the capability on one path rather than widening it further: the strip is required on the promote path and advisory on the rollback path (requireStrip at scripts/config/promote.mjs:39-48), so a failed deletion during recovery is now a warning carried on the result rather than a refusal, and rollback can no longer be blocked by a property of the release it restores. The promote path still refuses, pinned at scripts/config/tests/promote.test.mjs:186.

The spawn containment recorded in the previous revision stands and was not weakened: python3 runs with -I (scripts/config/validate.mjs:50), every checker runs with shell:false, a PATH-only environment (checkerEnvironment at :313-316), a freshly created empty working directory (openSandbox at :318-324, passed as cwd at :346), a 15s timeout and a 256KiB output cap (:349-350), and the command is re-checked against the frozen CHECKER_COMMANDS set at :338-343 before spawnSync at :344. Two residual exposures on that spawn are disclosed here rather than fixed in this round. First, checkerEnvironment passes the inherited PATH through unchanged, so an attacker-writable ABSOLUTE entry already on PATH hijacks every checker: `node`, `python3`, `bash`, `sh` and `zsh` are all resolved through it by spawnSync. Relative PATH elements are already neutralised because the checker's cwd is the empty mkdtemp sandbox, not the release. Pinning PATH to a fixed list of system directories would close it and is not attempted here. Second, the resolved hook path is realpath'd at :295 and then passed to spawnSync at :344, so a same-user rename or replace between those two calls is checked at one path and executed at another. Closing it needs fd-based checking that node does not expose (no openat/fexecve binding, and spawnSync takes a path, not a descriptor), so it is accepted rather than mitigated. Neither exposure reaches G5's stated escalation condition: no network-named command is invoked and no argument is credential-shaped.
